<security_assessment>
<decision>SAFE</decision>
<details>
The PKGBUILD fetches prebuilt Telegram Desktop binaries from the official GitHub repository (github.com/telegramdesktop/tdesktop) via a versioned release URL (`tsetup.${pkgver}.tar.xz`). This is standard practice for `-bin` packages in the AUR. The source URLs are legitimate and point to the project's own release artifacts and assets. All checksums are provided and non-skipped, ensuring integrity verification of the downloaded files.

The build process consists of standard packaging operations: installing binaries, icons, desktop files, and KDE protocol handlers into appropriate directories under `$pkgdir`. It removes RPATH from the binary using `chrpath`, which is a common hardening step for binary packages. It also disables the built-in updater by placing a configuration file in the expected directory, ensuring updates go through the package manager instead — a typical and safe practice for AUR packages.

No suspicious commands (e.g., `curl|bash`, `wget`, `eval`, obfuscated scripts) are present. There are no network operations during build or install, no data exfiltration, and no execution of downloaded code. The package conflicts with and provides `telegram-desktop`, following standard naming conventions. All actions are consistent with safe, conventional AUR packaging.
</details>
<summary>

<details>
The provided file is a standard `.desktop` file used by desktop environments on Linux systems to integrate applications into the application menu and handle URL protocols. LLM auditresponse for tg.protocol:
<security_assessment>
<decision>SAFE</decision>
<details>
The provided file is a desktop protocol handler configuration for Telegram Desktop, defining how the system should handle `tg://` URLs. It specifies that the `/usr/bin/telegram-desktop` binary should be executed with the URL as an argument. This is standard behavior for protocol handlers in desktop environments (e.g., GNOME, KDE) and aligns with expected functionality for applications that register custom URI schemes.

The configuration file follows the common `.protocol` or `.desktop` format used by XDG-compliant systems. All fields are legitimate and minimal: `exec`, `protocol`, `input`, `output`, etc., are correctly set for a helper protocol that does not perform file operations or data transfer directly. The settings `reading=false`, `writing=false`, `makedir=false`, and `deleting=false` indicate no filesystem access is claimed, which is appropriate for a messaging app's URL handler.

There is no executable code, obfuscation, network request, or suspicious command invocation in this file. It does not introduce any supply-chain risk, backdoor, or unintended behavior. The file serves a declarative purpose only and depends entirely on the security of the already-installed `telegram-desktop` binary, which is outside the scope of this assessment. No data exfiltration or remote execution is possible through this file alone.
</details>
<summary>
Standard protocol handler, no malicious content
</summary>
</security_assessment>
